text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: streaming.delta-route p99 latency crossed SLO (p99 > 6s) and live streaming stalls observed. Auto-created thread in #incidents. Paging: @emma oncall.

emma: ack. I'm looking. Any customer impact flagged?

raj: seeing p95 ~2s -> spike to p99 ~9s around 12:02 UTC, concurrent streaming connections per proxy also shot up. Metric window shows client side timeouts and re-tries.

oliver: confirmed — proxy logs show a large number of partial chunk payloads followed by connection close. nginx proxy_read_timeout hits and then clients reconnect, causing tail amplification.

sarah: customer-facing: support-bot reports 3 paid customers opened tickets citing duplicated messages and failed streaming sessions since ~11:58 UTC. Possibly mobile SDKs are more affected.

pm-lina: can we do a quick customer impact assessment? Which accounts are on streaming tailing?

emma: support-bot — paste last 10 ticket ids and top accounts.

support-bot: Tickets: #4521, #4523, #4526. Top accounts: acme-inc, wonderai, quickchat. All using SSE client with chunked transfers.

raj: initial hypothesis: recent config roll that decreased proxy buffer size + `proxy_read_timeout` lowered in canary earlier today. Devops PR 4827. If proxy_read_timeout too small, partial chunks get buffered and then connection closed.

oliver: pulling canary deploy diff now: https://git.repo/redwood/proxy/PR/4827 - I see `proxy_buffer_size` changed from 16k -> 8k and `proxy_read_timeout` from 60s -> 15s.

emma: roll forward mitigation options: 1) revert proxy change, 2) route streaming traffic to fallback streaming pool (older proxy config), 3) temporarily disable streaming chunked mode and fall back to polling/non-streaming for impacted customers.

sarah: customers prefer no polling fallback. Start with routing to fallback pool if possible.

raj: I can flip routing policy to send delta-route streaming to dedicated fallback cluster (fallback-stream-01) with prev config. Doing it now: `/infra route set delta-route fallback-stream-01 --immediate`

oncall-bot: Command accepted. Routing change enqueued.

emma: while routing switch is in progress, can we increase proxy_read_timeout globally to 45s to reduce immediate disconnects, and bump proxy_buffer_size to 32k?

oliver: I'm on the proxy nodes. Applying quick patch to canary proxies now. Patch:```nginx
proxy_buffer_size 32k;
proxy_read_timeout 45s;
```

raj: applied to canary. Monitoring metrics.

emma: status update in 2 mins. Also let's add a guard to autoscaler to prevent scaling down streaming headrooms for next 30m.

raj: autoscaler hold set for 30m. `/infra autoscaler hold streaming-headroom 30m`

oncall-bot: Autoscaler hold active.

(90s later)

oliver: routing change completed to fallback-stream-01. Canary proxies with increased timeouts show decreased connection closes. p99 dropped from 9s -> 3.1s. Still above target but trending down.

emma: good. Keep monitoring. Raj, can you run a tcpdump on an affected proxy for a sample SSE session to confirm chunk flush behavior? Capture for 60s on port 443.

raj: running tcpdump: `tcpdump -i eth0 port 443 -w /tmp/stream-sample.pcap` — will upload shortly.

support-bot: Notifying affected customers: simple template sent to acme-inc and quickchat with temporary mitigation note and ETA 1h.

pm-lina: please include apology and note we have mitigations in place routing traffic and increasing timeouts. Will follow up with full RCA.

emma: next actions: 1) keep traffic on fallback cluster until we can safely revert proxy PR, 2) prepare rollback of PR 4827, 3) gather logs + pcap for RCA, 4) coordinate customer comms. Assign: raj->pcap+logs, oliver->rollback PR, sarah->customer updates, emma->incident lead and timeline.

oliver: opening rollback PR now to revert buffer/timeouts change. `/git revert -m 1 4827 && /deploy proxy canary`

oncall-bot: Deploy triggered: proxy-canary-revert at 12:12 UTC.

(10m later)

raj: uploaded pcap and proxy logs to incident bucket s3://incidents/2187654321/ — found repeated `RST, ACK` from client after partial chunk delivery. Also observed upstream latency spikes correlated with one GPU host hitting high CPU steal (kube node n1-node-22).

emma: interesting — two factors: proxy config made socket handling brittle and a backend node resource issue amplified latency. We should cordon n1-node-22 and drain.

raj: cordoning and draining node now: `kubectl cordon n1-node-22 && kubectl drain n1-node-22 --ignore-daemonsets --force`

oliver: proxy canary revert successful, rolled out to canary then staged to 20% of edge. p99 now 2.1s on canary, overall p99 across global ~2.9s.

sarah: customers updated: emails sent to top 3 with link to status page. No escalations yet.

pm-lina: marking incident as "mitigating" and will prepare external summary for impacted customers after RCA.

emma: thanks team. Leaving routing on fallback until 1) revert fully deployed to all proxies and 2) node drain completes and we see stable p99 < 1.2s for 15m.

rajt: ack (typo).

raj: node drained, replaced pods scheduled to healthier nodes. Monitoring shows backend latencies normalized.

oliver: full revert deployed to 100% of edge proxies. p99 recovered to 1.0s, p95 ~0.5s.

emma: great. Rolling back routing to primary pool now. `/infra route set delta-route primary-stream --immediate`

oncall-bot: Routing change complete. Incident auto-note: mitigation applied, SLO recovered.

sarah: customer follow-ups queued. Recommend proactive postmortem with RCA on two contributing factors (proxy config and node resource issue) + runbook updates to prevent simultaneous config changes and autoscaler downscales.

emma: Agreed. Assigning postmortem owner: @emma. Timeline: preliminary RCA within 24h, full postmortem with remediation plan in 72h.

pm-lina: I'll draft customer-facing summary once RCA draft is available.

support-bot: Closing ticket if no further customer follow-ups.

emma: incident closed for now — will re-open if any regression. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
